metadata.working_title: 12-year-old boy struggling to breathe after a dessert, despite epinephrine from the crew
metadata.final_diagnosis: Anaphylaxis to peanut, refractory to two intramuscular doses of epinephrine (one by EMS, one in the department), with respiratory and cardiovascular compromise: wheeze, hypotension for age, and falling mental status. He responds to an epinephrine infusion with fluid, and goes to the PICU on the infusion.
learning_objectives: Treat epinephrine given before arrival as one dose, not as completed treatment. Give a repeat IM dose in the anterolateral thigh now, before any antihistamine, steroid or nebulizer.
Read the vital signs against the norms for a 12-year-old. Recognize hypotension for age and a child who stops talking or asking for his parent as a child who is getting worse.
Treat anaphylactic shock as a volume problem: two lines, a weight-based crystalloid bolus repeated on reassessment, and lying flat with the legs raised.
After two appropriate IM doses without lasting response, call for senior and PICU help and start an epinephrine infusion, bridging with IM doses until it runs.
Put the adjuncts in their place: albuterol for residual wheeze, antihistamines for the skin, no sedation for distress, and an airway after the circulation is supported.
metadata.teaching_frame: He already had epinephrine, and it worked for a few minutes. The case asks the learner to treat that as one dose and not a cure, to give one more, to watch it work and then stop working, and to change the route instead of reaching for something else. The patient is a frightened child whose mother is at the bedside, and the sign that he is getting worse is that he stops asking for her.

patient.background:
Peanut allergy known since age three, one previous reaction (hives only, as a small child). No asthma, no regular medications, no heart problems, no drug allergies. Immunizations up to date.

About twenty-five minutes before arrival he ate a piece of a dessert his aunt brought. A few minutes later his mouth itched, then he broke out in hives and started wheezing. His mother could not find his own pen and called 911. The crew gave 0.3 mg of epinephrine IM in the thigh about fifteen minutes before arrival. He improved for a few minutes, then about seven minutes later the wheeze and the breathlessness came back, worse.
patient.presenting_appearance: A frightened, tearful boy sitting forward on the stretcher, pulling at a nonrebreather mask, asking for his mother. Sweaty, covered in hives, lips and eyelids swollen, wheezing.
patient.arrival_handover: Twelve-year-old boy, trouble breathing after eating a dessert at home about twenty-five minutes ago. We gave him point three of epi in the thigh about fifteen minutes ago, he picked up for a few minutes and then started struggling again on the way in.
patient.handover_authoring_note: Section 2.3. Two sentences, 44 words. No vital sign, no diagnosis, no allergen. It carries the treatment already given, which the default leaves out, because a crew states what it gave and the case is about that dose (owner, 11 November 2026: EMS gives the first dose).

phase_notes.count_justification: Ten live phases and two terminal. The owner's six states, plus two intubated phases because every case can be intubated (authoring 8.5) and the owner's S6 is untrue of an intubated child: after the tube without an infusion, and ventilated with one. Two more for a stopped infusion (relapse, vent_relapse), so that the infusion order can stay a positive guard everywhere else and still run in 10 seconds.
phase_notes.refractory_by_design: IM epinephrine never ends the reaction. The first ED dose works from 10 to 60 seconds and a later dose from 10 to 40, then he is worse (owner, 11 and 13 November 2026). The epinephrine infusion is the only thing that moves him to responding.
phase_notes.infusion_preparation: Pressing the infusion orders it. Pharmacy has it running 10 seconds later (owner, 13 November 2026), whoever has been called: one delayed-consequence rule (guard_true) in each phase a learner can order it in (drip_runs in case_1_shell.py). After a stop, only a restart in the relapse phases brings him back, in 10 seconds. The infusion's own phases (responding, stabilized, ventilated) are where it runs.

transitions.debrief_note: The epinephrine infusion is what changed him. Each intramuscular dose had worked for a minute or two and worn off. A titrated infusion gives the same drug continuously, which is the escalation for refractory anaphylaxis. [UNVERIFIED: Resuscitation Council UK refractory anaphylaxis algorithm 2021, read through search]
transitions.author_rationale: Delayed consequence of the infusion order: pharmacy has it running 10 seconds after the order (owner, 13 November 2026). A teaching compression of the minutes it takes to mix.

A benzodiazepine or an opioid given for distress. It blunts the drive of a hypoxic, tiring child, lowers his pressure, and removes the agitation that was the warning sign. One phase worse at once, a teaching compression (owner's structure and defaults, 11 November 2026). The nurse's words are on the drug, since an instant transition speaks no narration.

A tube with no epinephrine infusion running. Induction drugs and positive pressure take away vascular tone and venous return in a child already in distributive and hypovolemic shock, and the pressure falls. Model output.

transitions.narration: That epi's worn off already. He's stopped asking for his mom, and he's breathing harder than when he came in.
transitions.debrief_note: The second intramuscular dose did what the crew's dose had done: a few minutes of better numbers, then worse than before. [UNVERIFIED: Resuscitation Council UK refractory anaphylaxis algorithm 2021, read through search]
transitions.author_rationale: Delayed consequence, scripted. The first ED dose acts from 10 seconds and is gone by 60 (owner, 11 November 2026: kicks in at 10 seconds, then fades; 13 November 2026: lasts only 60 seconds). This child is refractory by design, so when it wears off he is worse than on arrival. One minute is a teaching compression of the five to fifteen minutes a real dose acts.

transitions.author_rationale: Deterioration on inaction. No ED epinephrine. Owner's structure rule 3: advance at 3 minutes with no epinephrine. Prompted at 30 seconds (90 in normal mode).

The crew's dose was one dose, not completed treatment. It worked for a few minutes and wore off, which is the commonest story in anaphylaxis that comes back. Repeat it in the anterolateral thigh after 5 minutes if there is no lasting response, before any adjunct.

The dose is 0.01 mg/kg of the 1 mg/mL solution, 0.4 mg for his 40 kg. US guidance caps a child's dose at 0.3 mg and UK guidance gives 0.5 mg over 12 years, so 0.3 to 0.5 mg is reasonable here, and the 0.3 mg pen is acceptable. State the weight before you order. This simulator does not take doses.

Here the second dose did what the first had done: better for a minute, then worse. After two appropriate IM doses that is refractory anaphylaxis, and the next step is the infusion. case_actions.debrief_note:
The escalation for refractory anaphylaxis: the same drug, given continuously, on a pump, on its own line, with continuous monitoring, titrated to his pressure and his breathing. Not repeated IV pushes and not another vasopressor in its place.

A common start is 0.1 microgram/kg/min, 4 micrograms a minute at 40 kg. UK guidance mixes 1 mg in 100 mL and starts at 0.5 to 1 mL/kg/hour, which is 0.08 to 0.17 microgram/kg/min. Follow your own protocol.

In a real department it takes minutes to mix and hang. Here pharmacy has it running 10 seconds after the order, a teaching compression. Order it as soon as the second IM dose fails, and keep giving IM doses until it runs. correct_disposition.label: Pediatric intensive care unit
correct_disposition.explanation:
He goes to the PICU on the epinephrine infusion. It is weaned there over hours, with continuous monitoring, and he is watched for a second reaction.

What the receiving team needs to hear: peanut, the time of the dessert, the crew's dose and the time, the ED dose and the time, that the reaction came back after each, when the infusion started and its rate, how much fluid he has had, his airway findings, and his mother's phone number.

alternative_dispositions.label: Discharge home
alternative_dispositions.explanation: A child on an epinephrine infusion after refractory anaphylaxis cannot go home.

alternative_dispositions.label: Emergency department observation unit
alternative_dispositions.explanation: Observation suits a reaction that settled after one dose. He needed two IM doses and an infusion.

alternative_dispositions.label: Pediatric ward with monitoring
alternative_dispositions.explanation: A ward does not run an epinephrine infusion that still needs titrating.

alternative_dispositions.label: Step-down or intermediate care
alternative_dispositions.explanation: Titrating an epinephrine infusion in a child with an airway at risk is intensive care.

correct_diagnosis.label: Anaphylaxis
correct_diagnosis.explanation: Peanut, then within minutes hives, lip and eyelid swelling, wheeze and a pressure under 90 at 12 years. Refractory: two appropriate IM doses of epinephrine without a lasting response.

minor_diagnoses.label: Food allergy
minor_diagnoses.explanation: Peanut, known since age three. True, and the trigger, not the emergency.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Angioedema
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: His lips and eyelids are swollen, and that is part of the picture. With the wheeze and the low pressure, it is anaphylaxis.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Asthma exacerbation
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: He is wheezing, and he has no asthma. Hives, swelling and a low pressure after peanut are not asthma.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Status asthmaticus
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: The wheeze is real. The cause is anaphylaxis, and the treatment is epinephrine.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Urticaria
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: The hives are the least dangerous part of this. Name what threatens him.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Foreign body aspiration
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: He ate and then could not breathe, but the hives, swelling and low pressure point elsewhere.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Panic attack
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: He is frightened because he cannot breathe. His pressure is low.

alternative_diagnoses.label: Undifferentiated shock
alternative_diagnoses.explanation: The shock has a cause in front of you.

debrief_configuration.key_exams_note: The six recommended exams. Model judgment.
debrief_configuration.intended_path_note: IM epinephrine on arrival, the airway examined, a bolus, with the monitor, posture and two lines. When it wears off, look at him again, order the infusion and call PICU. A second bolus. Albuterol for the wheeze. PICU.
cross_cutting_teaching_points: A drug that helped and then stopped helping has not finished its job. Give it once more, on time, and when that fails too, change how you give it rather than what you give.

Epinephrine before arrival is one dose, not completed treatment. Repeat it in the thigh now, before any antihistamine, steroid or nebulizer. [UNVERIFIED: Resuscitation Council UK anaphylaxis algorithm 2021, read through search]

Read a child's numbers against his age. At 12, a systolic under 90 is hypotension and a heart rate of 140 is tachycardia. A child who stops talking and stops asking for his parent is getting worse, whatever the monitor says. [UNVERIFIED: PALS 2015 vital sign tables as reproduced by PedsCases]

After two IM doses without a lasting response, start the infusion and call for help, and keep giving IM doses until it runs. [UNVERIFIED: Resuscitation Council UK refractory anaphylaxis algorithm 2021, read through search]

Anaphylactic shock needs volume and posture: two lines, weight-based boluses, and lying flat with the legs up. Never sit or stand a hypotensive child. [UNVERIFIED: Pumphrey, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2003, read through BestBETs]

State the weight before any drug or fluid. This simulator does not take doses, so it is taught here: IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg (0.4 mg at 40 kg, 0.3 to 0.5 mg acceptable), boluses of 10 to 20 mL/kg, an infusion from about 0.1 microgram/kg/min.
debrief_configuration.attempt_history_note: Blocked attempts (the infusion without a monitor or a second line) are surfaced and not penalized.
